name: Learn brush lettering
blurb: Modern brush script: thin upstrokes, thick downstrokes, done with a flexible brush pen. Instantly attractive results and a shallow learning curve.
gear: A small brush pen (Tombow Fudenosuke or similar) and a larger one
Smooth paper — textured paper destroys brush tips
steps: Learn the core rule: light pressure going up, heavy pressure coming down. Everything else is application.
Drill basic strokes for a week: upstrokes, downstrokes, overturns, underturns, compound curves and ovals.
Learn the lowercase alphabet built from those strokes, one letter family at a time.
Learn connections between letters, which is where most beginner work falls apart.
Learn to letter a whole word, then a phrase, planning the layout first in pencil.
Add flourishes and bounce lettering once the basics are consistent.
tips: Rough paper shreds brush tips within days. Use smooth, dense paper.
Slow, deliberate strokes. Brush lettering done quickly looks shaky, not fluent.
proof: A lettered phrase with clean thick-thin contrast and consistent connections, on a card you would give someone.
